site.name: Michael Grigoryan
site.lede: Cities that were never built, drawn as if seen from everywhere at once.

hero.caption: «Մայիս» — first pencil line to finished sheet.
hero.alt: Time-lapse of the drawing «Մայիս» being made, from pencil construction lines to finished colour.

works.title: «Մայիս»
works.medium: Ink, marker and gouache on paper
works.alt: A steep town of stacked coloured houses and a tall striped smokestack trailing dark smoke, set between snow-capped mountains under a pale green sky streaked with pink.

works.title: «Հանգիստ»
works.medium: Ink, marker and gouache on paper
works.alt: A steep harbour village of red, coral and ochre houses stacked above a stone quay, with small boats on turquoise water and a sky of magenta and violet ribbons.

works.title: «Երևան»
works.medium: Ink, marker and gouache on paper
works.alt: A spring street scene under a burning red and pink sky with Armenian lettering in the clouds: yellow, red and blue houses, blossoming trees, an antique shop, and two figures walking a pale road.

works.title: «Սուրբ Աննա»
works.medium: Ink, marker and gouache on paper
works.alt: An old quarter with a domed church, scaffolding and chimney smoke, drawn from a tilted overhead viewpoint beneath a sky of amber and gold bands.

works.title: «Կիրակի»
works.medium: Ink, marker and gouache on paper
works.alt: A densely packed town seen from above at a tilt, tiled roofs and facades folding into one another, with a band of blue patterned water along the top edge.

works.title: «Քաղաք»
works.medium: Ink, marker and gouache on paper
works.alt: A crowded painted town of brick and tile with a red and white striped circus tent at one edge, shop signs, a garage and a hotel, beneath a pale sky of rose and grey ribbons.

about.opening: A city is a thing you can only ever see part of at a time. Michael Grigoryan draws all of it at once.
paragraphs: > Yerevan is a pink city. Pink is my favourite colour and Yerevan is my favourite city, and I can make the city even more colourful, even pinker — and hide a lot of secrets and small things inside the picture.

His streets lean toward you and away from you in the same breath. Roofs pile onto roofs. A staircase climbs, thinks better of it, and turns back into the wall it came from. There is no single place to stand in these pictures, which is the point: they are how a city sits in memory rather than how it sits on a map.

Nothing is left blank. Every roof is counted out tile by tile, every wall brick by brick, and when the buildings run out the sky takes the job on — not as air but as ribbon, flat bands of magenta and violet and ochre laid over the town like a lid. Stay with a picture and it starts handing things over: a cat on a parapet, washing strung between windows, a pear tree with no business being there, an antique shop with its sign in Armenian, a boy crossing an empty road while nobody watches.
Everything begins in pencil — the perspective, the roof lines, the run of the street — and is then filled in, block by block, until no paper is left showing.

> I was impressed by Egon Schiele. His work is very different from mine — darker, different — but it stayed with me. That, and my love for Yerevan, is why I started to draw my favourite picture. The city was the start of my style, and of the line. I want to continue the line. I have found the style that is mine.

Michael Grigoryan (b. 2002) lives and works in Yerevan. He studied at the State Academy of Fine Arts of Armenia, graduating in 2024 with a degree in computer graphics, and works as a graphic and web designer alongside the drawings. The training is visible in the flat colour and the constructed compositions. Everything else is done by hand, at close range, without shortcuts.
